name: Woodtech
old_description: Datatek's origins date back to 1988 when we began making blue line prints for the architectural/engineering trades under the name of Alabama Blueprint & Supply Co, Inc. Moving forward with changes in digital technology, the little company traded the ammonia-vapor "blue-print" machines for state-of-the-art digital printers. The change resulted in increased capabilities and additional job positions. The company has continued its growth in the local market and is the oldest operating full-service reprographic company in the region.
about:
Woodtech, a division of Datatek, operates from Huntsville, Alabama. Datatek was founded in 1988 as Alabama Blueprint & Supply Co., Inc., producing blue line prints for architects and engineers. In early 2014, Datatek launched Woodtech to merge its digital printing capabilities with fine woodworking, opening a showroom and retail center in downtown Huntsville's Clinton Row Project.

The company provides CNC machining, digital flatbed printing, and custom woodworking services, producing signage, furniture, inlays, overlays, home décor, and gift items. A polyurethane coating is applied to protect finished pieces. Through 2015, the division added five positions—four in production and design and one in sales—though total headcount is not disclosed.

Woodtech serves construction, architecture, engineering, real estate, fine art, photography, education, and hospitality sectors, as well as retail brands seeking custom merchandise. Local artists and photographers supply much of the imagery used on products, and the company partners with Swampworks Amplifiers for custom-printed amplifier cabinets.

The business emphasizes local material sourcing: with the exception of plywood, all wood comes from Madison County and the North Alabama region, reclaimed from naturally fallen trees or necessary removals. This regional focus, combined with digital-print-to-wood workflows, distinguishes the division from conventional sign shops.
